entities.name: Insulinoma
observations: Fasting hypoglycemia with inappropriately detectable insulin, C-peptide, and proinsulin plus suppressed beta-hydroxybutyrate supports endogenous hyperinsulinism; insulinoma is the leading listed diagnosis if secretagogue exposure is excluded.

entities.name: Sulfonylurea-induced hypoglycemia
observations: Sulfonylurea exposure can reproduce the biochemical pattern of insulinoma and requires a plasma or urine secretagogue screen during hypoglycemia.

entities.name: Hypopituitarism
observations: Pituitary hormone deficiency may cause non-insulin-mediated hypoglycemia, but isolated hypopituitarism does not explain inappropriately present insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, and suppressed beta-hydroxybutyrate in the critical sample.

entities.name: NIPHS
observations: NIPHS generally causes predominantly postprandial hypoglycemia and is less likely than insulinoma in a patient with fasting hypoglycemia.

entities.name: Endogenous hyperinsulinism
observations: At glucose 54 mg/dL, insulin was 29 pmol/L, C-peptide 272 pmol/L, proinsulin 8 pmol/L, and beta-hydroxybutyrate 1.2 mmol/L, indicating insulin-mediated endogenous hypoglycemia.
